newsitem.title: HONG KONG: INTERVIEW-CITIC sees CLP as better option.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-CITIC sees CLP as better option.

text.p: The shift of CITIC Pacific Ltd's investment to China Light & Power Co Ltd (CLP) from its stake in Hongkong Telecom is a better option for the firm, its managing director Henry Fan said on Monday.
Fan said CITIC Pacific's 20 percent stake in CLP could be equity accounted while CITIC Pacific took part in the power concern's executive committee and had a say in the management.

"In (Hongkong) Telecom we only hold 7.74 percent, which cannot be equity accounted. Therefore even when we sold (Telecom shares) at HK$12.60 we would be selling at about 17 times P/E (price/earnings ratio)," he said.
Fan said the calculation of P/E on the stake was based on dividend rather than earnings per share since the stake was regarded as a pure investment rather than investment in an associate.
The Hong Kong-based conglomerate has agreed to sell its stake in Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd for HK$11.4 billion.
Earlier this year, the company paid HK$16.25 billion, or about HK$32.60 a share, for 20 percent of CLP.
Fan said CITIC estimated that CLP's joint venture property project with Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd in Hunghom's Huk Un Street was worth about HK$3.54 a share.
Another HK$4.00 or so would be for the hidden or unrealised property redevelopment potential of China Light and about HK$6.30 would be cash from the proceeds by issuing new shares to CITIC Pacific.
"Our money went into the company and we automatically will get 20 pecent of that," Fan said.
After deducting all that from the price CITIC Pacific had paid, it ended up paying HK$18.00-HK$19.00 a share or less than 10 times P/E for CLP's core business in Hong Kong.
But the price did not take into account projects in China and overseas.
"Then it's getting Daya Bay, Shandong, India, etc, for free and getting Shenzhen for free," he said.

Fan also said CITIC Pacific's investment in Hongkong Telecom had been diluted from 8.0 percent to 7.74 percent since Telecom introduced a script dividen option 18 months ago because his company opted for cash dividend.
"So we are getting constantly diluted and if we don't sell it now three, five years down the road our earnings would be further eroded," the managing director said.
"If you look at all these factors, you would agree that instant sale out is indeed a better option," he said.
